culprit_citations.quoted_text: Raw schedule hierarchy row is separate: Debt Investments - 226.3 %; extracted issuer names in the bundle include hierarchy prefixes such as United States - 205.6% 1st Lien/Senior Secured Debt - 195.3% Acquia, Inc.
Raw investment row is Acquia, Inc. | Software | 9.59 % | S + 5.50 % | 10/30/26 | 42,164 | 41,960 | 41,743 | (7) (8), not a hierarchy-prefixed issuer name.

findings.detail: Issuer identity is contaminated with schedule hierarchy labels and percentages, which can break cross-period issuer continuity even when the raw issuer persists.

citation.quoted_text: Acquia, Inc. appears as the raw investment name, while the bundle's extracted issuer sample prefixes it with United States and lien-category hierarchy text.

rationale: D06 is an aggregate continuity flag (47/123 issuers persist, metric 0.382 below threshold 0.5). The filing totals are readable and tie at the schedule level: Total Investments at fair value is 3,261,721 for 2025 and 3,475,258 for 2024. The defect localizes through the row-disposition structure: raw schedule hierarchy rows such as Debt Investments and country/lien-category rows are separate from investment rows, but the reviewed extract sample stores those hierarchy labels inside issuer_name. A named source example confirms Acquia, Inc. is the raw issuer row, while the bundle's extracted issuer format prefixes Acquia, Inc. with United States and lien-category text. That source-backed issuer contamination makes the low continuity flag a real extraction data error rather than a false alarm.
